name: Cloudy Blue
lede: Cloudy blue is a descriptive color name, a soft grey-blue, and our books use it as a plain phrase rather than a named pigment.

sections.title: An everyday phrase
sections.body:
The books give no pigment, dye or maker behind the name. In Bluets, Nelson uses the phrase for the water at the bottom of a swimming pool, lit by white winter light, in a passage of ordinary things that are blue [1]. Cloudy blue is a description of what the eye sees, with no history behind it.

As a swatch it is a pale, greyed blue, next to [[light-grey-blue]], [[sky-blue]] and [[light-blue]], all of them paler and softer than plain [[blue]]. Our library traces the name to ISCC-NBS (1955) and to the xkcd color survey of 2010 [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color appears in 163 of 23,781 archive paintings, 0.69 per cent, more common than 62 per cent of named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1800s, in 67 of 8,345 paintings, 1.5 times the museums' baseline [2]. In 45 per cent of the 119 paintings where it shows up inside the picture, it is a hidden color [2]. All of this is as photographed.
